topic: Hidden detail: Gaban's line in 1194 makes Zoro the third pupil in a chain of Roger Pirates teachers
title: Gaban's Quiet Gift To Zoro (One Piece 1194)
description: Everyone is talking about Mihawk in chapter 1194, but Gaban's few words did just as much. Here's why that matters for Zoro's future.
comment: Who shaped Zoro more, Mihawk or Gaban? Pick one.

lines.text: Everyone credits Mihawk for Zoro's breakthrough. Nobody talks about Gaban.
Chapter 1194. Zoro can't control his Supreme King Haki, and Sommers keeps regenerating.
But the real shift is Gaban's line.

shot.fallback: old pirate talking to a swordsman

lines.text: Gaban admits he never knew he had Supreme King Haki himself.
Think about that. A Roger Pirate carried it his whole life and never knew.

shot.fallback: old pirate crew on a ship

lines.text: Zoro didn't just get a lesson. He got the proof you can lose it by never believing it.

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman with dark aura

lines.text: Sure, Mihawk gets the credit because he's the famous teacher.
But Mihawk gave him the technique. Gaban gave him the permission.

shot.fallback: two fighters nodding to each other

lines.text: And that's the part I think Oda planted on purpose.

shot.fallback: swordsman looking at a stormy sky

lines.text: Here is my read: Zoro won because two old legends handed him what they never used.

shot.fallback: swordsman coating swords in black lightning

lines.text: Everyone credits Mihawk for Zoro's breakthrough...
